title: CCTC Release Targets Manifest
description: Per-repo binding between the canonical, tool-agnostic build-target contract (documented in claude-org guides/build-and-release.md) and this repo's actual build commands. The org release automation reads this manifest and never hardcodes a repo's paths or tools. Which targets are mandatory depends on the repo's regulatory_tier and is checked separately (scripts/release/contract.py), not by this schema.

build_tool.description: Informational: the build tool this manifest drives (e.g. FAKE, MSBuild, Cake, npm, Make). Not used for binding — the commands in `targets` are authoritative.

version_pin_env.description: Name of the environment variable the build honours to pin the version it stamps (so CI can build the exact version a tag names rather than a self-computed one). The `version` target must respect it.

images.description: For hosted apps that ship one or more container images: the set of component images this repo builds, keyed by component name (e.g. trialview, trialview-api). The build's `package` target produces all of them and `publish:registry` pushes each; the workflow attests and references each independently, and the on-server agent pins each digest. A single-image repo declares one entry. Omit entirely for repos whose distributable is a package (nupkg/zip) rather than an image.

repository.description: Image repository path within the registry, e.g. cctc-team/trialview.

digest_env.description: Environment variable the `publish:registry` target writes THIS image's pushed sha256 digest into, so the workflow can attest and reference that exact digest and the agent can pin it. Each image needs its own.

sbom.description: Optional glob(s) for the CycloneDX SBOM file the `sbom` target produces for THIS image, so the workflow can attest the SBOM to this specific image digest.

targets.description: Map from canonical target name to how this repo invokes it. Keys are restricted to the canonical target vocabulary; presence of the mandatory ones for this repo's regulatory_tier is enforced by scripts/release/contract.py.

run.description: The command this repo runs to satisfy the target. The org workflow executes it verbatim; nothing about it is interpreted by the workflow.

outputs.description: Optional glob(s) for the files this target produces, so the workflow can collect them (e.g. the validation report or SBOM path).
